correctness.rationale: For every real symmetric stochastic flux, spectral norm is at most one, so I-r Phi^2 is positive definite. The exact next-generation matrix is r Phi^2+r(zeta-1)(Phi e)(Phi e)^T. Rank-one congruence gives the necessary-and-sufficient scalar threshold; eigenbasis decomposition yields the M(1-r) constant term and the explicitly weighted spectral energy, and Rayleigh/constant row sums prove optimality and its equality case. Exact inverse computation gives H=529543/11008272>1/24 and 245/5956<1/24 for two admissible rational five-patch networks with identical hub columns. The extracted standalone SymPy checker reruns all identities and exact arithmetic. Finite checking corroborates but does not replace the general proof; all positive-recovery and symmetry boundaries are stated.

originality.rationale: The principal new statement concerns the non-equitable, nonuniform-hub mobility case: an exact spectral-heterogeneity threshold and a rigorously computed pair with the same full hotspot column but opposite invasion status. Das–Stolerman (2023, Sections 2–4) assumes uniform hub access in its threshold classes and conjectures; the 2019 equitable-quotient result applies to that uniform-column subclass but does not classify the nonuniform-column pair. General rank-one and Perron results are acknowledged as ingredients, not claimed novel. Searches and the accessible primary full text identified no directly covering result; a future comprehensive literature audit could find one.
residual_risks: The unrestricted rank-one secular criterion is classical; originality is restricted to this SIR-network spectral-energy formulation and its exact same-hub-column opposite-outcome pair.
Equitable quotient results predate the motivating paper and imply much of the uniform-hub subcase; that corollary is not offered as novel.
The complete text of the 2019 equitable-quotient paper was not obtained; later unpublished or unindexed literature might contain an equivalent nonuniform-hub criterion.
Other metapopulation papers were checked at abstract or relevant-section depth only; absence of a matching search result is not a novelty certificate.

value.rationale: Travel to and from a uniquely high-transmission hub is naturally observable, but the novel model-specific classification demonstrates it is not a sufficient statistic: two five-patch communities with exactly the same hub column and identical hub traffic variance fall on opposite sides of epidemic invasion solely because non-hub travel changes. The general spectral energy supplies an exact all-size threshold for arbitrary symmetric mobility, a rigorous optimum, and quantitative comparison to observed hub-column variance. It extends the source paper’s explicitly studied constant-hub-flux setting and resolves a motivated decision boundary rather than an arbitrary numerical case.
